root_causes: Inefficient high-level Rearrange commands that implicitly bundle navigation, pickup, and placement led to long, costly sequences before visible progress (first object not secured on bench until step 8).
Poor coordination between agents: one agent frequently executed Wait while still holding an object instead of assisting with remaining sub-tasks or freeing its hand early.

Object state management was suboptimal: agents continued to hold items (e.g., squeezer_1, toy_food_2, cup_0) even after reaching the bench instead of promptly placing them, causing extra steps and negative reward.
Replanning triggers (td_error_peak / replan windows) did not translate into more efficient strategies; the system persisted with similar long-horizon Rearrange actions despite high cost.
improvement_suggestions: Decompose Rearrange into explicit Navigate + PickUp + Place primitives so progress and errors are observable earlier and corrections are cheaper.
Improve multi-agent coordination: when one agent is idle (Wait) and holding an object, prioritize placing or handing off that object or assigning it another subgoal rather than waiting.
Introduce a policy to minimize time holding objects near the goal: once at the bench, immediately execute a Place action instead of continuing to carry the object through further planning steps.
Use replanning signals (td_error_peak, progress_change) to adjust strategy: shorten action horizons, adjust paths, or swap responsibilities between agents when progress is slow.
Add a cost-aware objective that explicitly penalizes long-running Rearrange actions and sustained Wait states, encouraging more direct and parallelized task completion.
overall_assessment: The task was completed successfully with all three items placed as required, but the trajectory showed inefficiencies in action decomposition and multi-agent coordination, leading to unnecessary waiting and elevated cumulative cost.
task_instruction: Put the mug, squeezer, and toy food on the bench in the entryway.
